quests.title: Rain Gauge Railway Route Visit
quests.visitSkill: Turn an optional adult choice into a map-based story route with a clear setting clue.
quests.visitFit: Upper-age adult-led printable quest for a calm visit table, library family table, or homeschool co-op family day.
quests.adultSetup: Print one page, set out pencils, and invite the adult helper to choose one invented weather object or railway stop.
quests.kidDirection: Use the helper's pretend choice to plan a rain-gauge railway route, then draft a short scene with a beginning, turn, and wrap.
quests.hostPrompt: Offer one invented object, station, or weather clue; all choices can be made up on the spot.

pageSections.heading: Visit story seed
lines: The visit table becomes a rainy railway when the helper chooses ____________________.
An ordinary object near the table turns into a station sign for ____________________.
The pretend weather note on the ticket warns about ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Talk-to-story choice
lines: Ask the helper to choose one invented railway job: ____________________.
The choice changes the route because ____________________.
The optional talk detail I will turn into a story clue is ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Tiny draft
lines: First, the rain-gauge train stops at ____________________.
Then the conductor notices ____________________.
The helper's choice changes the story by ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Visit wrap
lines: My favorite invented clue from the visit is ____________________.
One sentence I can make clearer is ____________________.
The ending leaves the railway near ____________________.

quests.quietOption: Quiet option: skip the talk choice and pick one printed object card: ____________________.
quests.takeHomeLine: Take-home line: Later, add one new pretend weather station called ____________________.

quests.title: Seed Library Map Room Catalog Visit
quests.visitSkill: Use an optional adult choice to connect a catalog clue, map mark, and next story action.
quests.visitFit: Upper-age adult-led printable quest for a relaxed visit, library family table, or homeschool co-op writing stop.
quests.adultSetup: Print the page, place three harmless object prompts nearby, and ask the adult helper to invent one drawer label or map direction.
quests.kidDirection: Choose a seed-library clue, add the helper's invented map choice, and write what the catalog helper does next.
quests.hostPrompt: Choose one pretend drawer label, path, color, or map mark; keep it invented and simple.

pageSections.heading: Visit story seed
lines: The map room drawer opens to ____________________.
The packet label describes a pretend plant that grows ____________________.
The helper's optional choice adds a map mark shaped like ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Talk-to-story choice
lines: Ask for one invented drawer category, then write ____________________.
Choose whether the seed helper follows a path, shelf, or return basket: ____________________.
The conversation detail I will turn into a story clue is ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Tiny draft
lines: The catalog helper opens ____________________.
The map changes when ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Visit wrap
lines: The strongest map-room clue is ____________________.
A word that makes the setting clearer is ____________________.
The story can continue when the packet reveals ____________________.

quests.quietOption: Quiet option: choose a printed drawer label and write the map clue here: ____________________.
quests.takeHomeLine: Take-home line: Add a new seed-library catalog card for ____________________.

quests.title: Revision River Ferry Keep Move Trim Visit
quests.visitSkill: Revise an invented ferry scene after an adult helper chooses one detail to keep, move, or trim.
quests.visitFit: Adult-led upper-age printable quest for a cooperative visit table where sharing is optional and revision stays low-pressure.
quests.adultSetup: Print the page, set out pencils, and offer three paper choices: keep a detail, move a detail, or trim a detail.
quests.kidDirection: Draft a ferry sentence, use the helper's invented revision choice, and rewrite one line so the ending is clearer.
quests.hostPrompt: Choose keep, move, or trim for one pretend ferry detail, then ask where that detail belongs in the ending.

pageSections.heading: Visit story seed
lines: The ferry carries a draft crate labeled ____________________.
The first dock shows a scene detail I might keep: ____________________.
The river sign points toward an ending about ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Talk-to-story choice
lines: Ask the helper to choose keep, move, or trim for this detail: ____________________.
The choice changes my next sentence by ____________________.
The detail that should echo near the ending is ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Tiny draft
lines: My first ferry sentence is ____________________.
I revise it by adding, moving, or trimming ____________________.
My clearer sentence becomes ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Visit wrap
lines: The revision move I used today is ____________________.
The story is easier to follow because ____________________.
The ferry can land at ____________________.

quests.quietOption: Quiet option: choose keep, move, or trim silently and mark the detail here: ____________________.
quests.takeHomeLine: Take-home line: Later, revise one more ferry sentence about ____________________.

quests.title: Clue Label Tower Exhibit Visit
quests.visitSkill: Select one precise clue and turn it into a concise invented exhibit label.
quests.visitFit: Adult-led upper-age printable quest for a visit table, library family station, or homeschool co-op display activity.
quests.adultSetup: Print the page, point to any safe ordinary object or printed object card, and invite the adult helper to choose one invented clue.
quests.kidDirection: Build a pretend tower exhibit, pick the clue that matters first, and draft a label that guides the reader into the scene.
quests.hostPrompt: Choose one color, shape, sound, texture, or object clue; the exhibit can be completely made up.

pageSections.heading: Visit story seed
lines: The tower exhibit holds an ordinary object called ____________________.
The clue label points readers toward ____________________.
The helper's invented clue is a color, shape, sound, or texture: ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Talk-to-story choice
lines: Ask the helper to choose which clue matters first: ____________________.
The clue I will leave in the background is ____________________.
The label should make visitors wonder about ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Tiny draft
lines: My exhibit label begins with ____________________.
The label explains the clue by saying ____________________.
The scene changes when a visitor notices ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Visit wrap
lines: The clearest label word is ____________________.
One extra detail I can save for later is ____________________.
The next exhibit in the tower could be ____________________.

quests.quietOption: Quiet option: skip discussion and write only the final exhibit label here: ____________________.
quests.takeHomeLine: Take-home line: Make a pretend label for one safe ordinary object: ____________________.
